facts.fact_text: In February-March 2003 a presidential election took place in Armenia.
Following the February-March 2003 presidential election in Armenia, the applicant participated in a series of rallies of protest organised in Yerevan by the opposition parties.
On 7 April 2003 at 5 p.m. a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 took place on the Mashtots Avenue next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան).
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature.
During the demonstration of 7 April 2003, criticism of the Government and of the conduct of the presidential election was voiced.

The applicant alleged that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003 in order to facilitate its conduct.

The Government did not dispute the applicant's allegation that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the march that followed the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
On 9 April 2003 at 12 noon another demonstration was organised in the same area (next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts on the Mashtots Avenue in Yerevan) by the opposition parties.
The demonstration of 9 April 2003 was followed by a march towards the Government building where the inauguration ceremony of the elected President was taking place.
The applicant was in the front line of the march of 9 April 2003, holding the Armenian flag.
According to the applicant, the march of 9 April 2003 was blocked at the very beginning of the Mashtots Avenue by special forces.
According to the applicant, since the demonstrators insisted on continuing their march on 9 April 2003, the special forces started to disperse the demonstration with rubber clubs.
According to the applicant, on her way home on 7 April 2003 she was approached by three men in civilian clothes who, without presenting themselves, started dragging her to a nearby car.
According to the applicant, the three men who approached her on 7 April 2003 twisted her arms, punched her and pushed her into the car.
According to the applicant, she screamed and tried to resist when the three men in civilian clothes attempted to drag her to a nearby car on 7 April 2003.
The applicant was taken to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժին).
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the applicant found out that she had been arrested for having participated in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest (արձանագրություն բերման ենթարկելու մասին).
The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant had been "arrested at 7.30 p.m. at 12 Khorhurdneri Street for violating public order".

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that the applicant was brought to the Central District Police Station for having participated on 7 April 2003 in an unauthorised march headed from the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) to the Constitutional Court and violated public order.

The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) in which it was stated that the applicant had "participated in a march and violated public order" on 7 April 2003.
The applicant's actions on 7 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – "the CAO") as minor hooliganism.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to an administrative fine of 1500 Armenian drams (approximately EUR 2.4 at the material time) in relation to the events of 7 April 2003.

Judge M.'s entire finding in relation to the events of 7 April 2003 stated: "On 7 April 2003 between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. ... on the Mashtots Avenue [the applicant], together with a group of people, obstructed street traffic, violated public order by making a loud noise, and incited other participants of the demonstration to do the same..."
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. threatened the applicant with imminent detention if she did not refrain from further participation in demonstrations.
According to the applicant, the march of 9 April 2003 was blocked at the very beginning of the Mashtots Avenue by special forces.
According to the applicant, since the demonstrators insisted on continuing their march on 9 April 2003, the special forces started to disperse the demonstration with rubber clubs.
According to the applicant, she was ordered by a police officer on 9 April 2003 to hand over the flag.
According to the applicant, she refused to hand over the flag on 9 April 2003, after which she was beaten and taken to a police car.
At around 2.30 p.m. on 9 April 2003 the applicant was brought to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.

The arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest on 9 April 2003 in which it was stated that she had been "arrested for having violated public order during the march of 9 April 2003".

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that during the march of 9 April 2003 after the demonstration next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) he noticed one citizen who was violating public order: waving a flag while walking on the driveway, obstructing the regular traffic of public transport, creating an emergency situation, randomly hitting passers-by who were not taking part in the demonstration with the long flagpole, and inciting others to follow her example.

The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence on 9 April 2003 in which it was stated that the applicant had "made a loud noise with a group of people, and randomly insulted and hit passers-by in the Central District".
The applicant's actions on 9 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) as minor hooliganism.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to five days of administrative detention in relation to the events of 9 April 2003.

Judge M.'s entire finding in relation to the events of 9 April 2003 stated: "On 9 April 2003 between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. in the Central District of Yerevan [the applicant], swearing loudly and hitting passers-by, obstructed street traffic and violated public order."

In deciding on the administrative penalty for the events of 9 April 2003, Judge M. took into account as an aggravating circumstance the repetition of the anti-social behaviour of 7 April 2003, i.e. re-commission of a similar offence within one year.
In deciding on the administrative penalty for the events of 9 April 2003, Judge M. took into account as an aggravating circumstance that the offence was committed by a group of people.

The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 9 April 2003, Judge M. asked the applicant: "if you promise in writing that from now on you will not participate in demonstrations and marches any more, I will fine you and let you go home, otherwise I will detain you".

The applicant replied to Judge M. at the court hearing of 9 April 2003 that she had participated and would continue to participate in demonstrations, because she had not violated any laws and nobody had the right to prohibit her from enjoying her constitutional rights.
Judge M. pronounced the sentence of five days of administrative detention at the court hearing of 9 April 2003.
Following the sentence pronounced by Judge M. on 9 April 2003, the applicant was taken to a detention centre where she served her sentence.
